messages:
incident-bot: Alert: SLO breach detected for streaming tail latency in us-west-2 (p99 > 2.5s) — triggering incident channel. Metric: tail_stream_latency.p99 = 2.94s :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Related alarms: cache_miss_rate.namespace=high, inflight_slowpath.p95 up 3x. Logs linked: https://logs.redwood/stream/3512345678
mira: seeing big p99 blips on dashboards, playback stalls for small segments. Customers reporting partial stream stalls.
sasha: timeline? any recent deploys or config changes?
raj: pushed namespace-salt rotation to edge routing 12:03 UTC (~30m ago) — rollout to 40% then auto-increment. No direct model changes.
mira: that aligns with when tail latency started climbing. Cache evictions spiked immediately after.
tim: digging into cache telemetry — prefix cache hitrate dropped from 92% -> 47% since 12:05. Most misses concentrated on the new salted namespace keyspace.
sasha: that would cause extra paging and KV reads, explains p95/p99 tail. Is there any partial fallback path that is heavier?
raj: yes, missed prefixes go to backing store + disk paging; that path has higher variance. Also stream handler does synchronous warmup which is slow.
mir a: (typo) mira: ^
alison-cs: we have 3 customer escalations in last 20m, mostly degraded quality for large doc walkthroughs. Two are on Dedicated tenants. CS flagged potential SLA impact.
mira: mitigation plan: 1) throttle the namespace-salt rollout (pause and roll back to 0%); 2) create temporary routing rule to prefer pre-salted caches for streaming; 3) increase short-term KV read parallelism; 4) notify customers. Thoughts?
sasha: agree rollback asap. Rollout control shows remaining nodes = 60% unrolled, but 40% already live. Need coordination with deploybot.
raj: initiating rollback now: 
```
# rollback namespace-salt rollout
deploybot rollback --change-name=ns-salt-rotation --to-group=0%
```
incident-bot: Deploybot: rollback job started by raj. Job ID dpl-98321. Estimated completion 3m.
tim: while rollback runs, we can flip routing to prefer legacy cache by setting env var on stream-proxy (hotfix): 
```
kubectl -n stream patch deployment stream-proxy -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"fix/prefer-legacy-cache":"true"}}}}}'
```
raj: applying hotfix now.

(3m pass)
incident-bot: Deploybot: rollback dpl-98321 completed successfully.
tim: routing patch applied across proxy replicas. Hitrate improved to ~78% within 90s, p95 dropped ~30%. p99 trending down but still elevated at 1.6s.
sasha: good. Any persistent hot shards or eviction waves?
tim: eviction wave still decaying — small set of hotkeys still miss because of misaligned salt mapping. I can kick an async cache-warm job for top 500 keys to smooth tail.
mira: do it. Also add temporary rate-limit to background warmups so we don't overload backing store.
tim: warming top-500 keys (async, backoff=200ms). Hitrate moved to 89% after warmups. p99 now 1.02s. p95 220ms.
alison-cs: sharing update to customers: "We identified a cache namespace mapping issue after a rollout; we paused the rollout and applied mitigations. Most requests should be back to normal; we're continuing warmups. We'll follow up with postmortem." Can post to affected tenants now?
sasha: yep go ahead. Include ETA for postmortem.
mira: handoff: i'll remain on until 13:30 UTC for monitoring and then handoff to night oncall (@sasha night shift). Please include all logs and the rollback job id in the handoff.
raj: added notes to incident doc: rollback dpl-98321, proxy patch annotation fix/prefer-legacy-cache=true, warmup job wup-3512.
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV-2: system functional, tail latency improving, customer impact limited to degraded quality window.
sasha: follow-ups: 1) revert namespace-salt rollout and add hold gate until we have a preflight hit-rate sim; 2) add automated canary for cache-hit delta detection (alert at >10% drop); 3) postmortem to include key distribution audit and deploy rollback playbook; 4) check Dedicated tenant configs — ensure separation in rollout policies.
mira: agreed. I'll open the postmortem and assign owners.
alison-cs: customers notified, one wants an incident timeline. I'll coordinate with you, mira.

(13:20 UTC)
mira: handing off to sasha for overnight watch. if p99 climbs above 1.5s or cache_miss_rate.namespace > 15% re-escalate to eng-sre.
sasha: taking over. tagging oncall rotation: @sasha oncall-night. Closing live bridge but keeping channel pinned for updates. :white_check_mark:
